title: What Comes Next After Anthropic’s Historic IPO
summary: Anthropic's $81 billion IPO, the largest ever and the first by an AI lab, has created more than 5,000 paper millionaires among employees, according to an estimate from Hill.com, and left backers such as Lightspeed and Iconiq with stakes worth over $25 billion at the IPO price. Investors expect the windfall to recycle into the AI ecosystem and spur a wave of AI IPOs next year, though questions remain about whether the stock can hold up against OpenAI and Chinese open-source rivals. Some venture investors warn the listing could push startup valuations higher and lead to wasted capital.

title: Put-Downs, Parties and a ‘Royal Family’: The Culture Inside Jensen Huang’s Nvidia
summary: A WSJ investigation describes how Nvidia, despite growing into a $5 trillion company, operated in many ways as a family business under ousted CEO Jensen Huang. Huang brought his two adult children, Madison and Spencer, into the company, and Madison Huang's husband also works there. The report adds to scrutiny of Nvidia's governance following Huang's departure and an SEC probe.

title: How Apple Got Caught Up in Google Search Ads Slowdown
summary: Google shares have fallen 18% since it reported a sharp slowdown in search ad revenue growth, driven partly by the popularity of its AI features. Apple, which receives a cut of Google's ad revenue from Safari searches, saw services revenue growth slow to 10% from 12% last quarter and expects further cooling. Reddit has also warned that AI-driven changes to Google search are reducing referral traffic to its forums.

title: Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive 11 days after he resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believed was linked to Chinese intelligence, saying senior U.S. government input left it confident his return poses no national-security risk. President Trump, who pushed for the move, praised the decision, and Nvidia shares jumped roughly 30% on Monday. The Information's Martin Peers argued Huang now owes his job to Trump, raising questions about what the administration may seek in return, such as an equity stake or a board seat.

title: Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia Draws Heavy Fire From Lawmakers
summary: Republican and Democratic lawmakers criticized Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang, citing national-security risks. Members of both parties said they intend to press ahead with their investigations into the chip maker and its CEO.

title: Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia. Major Investigations Still Surround Him.
summary: Despite his reinstatement, Jensen Huang and Nvidia remain the subject of several probes examining the company, its CEO and matters tied to his initial ouster. The inquiries include questions over his personal dealings and the company's alleged role in chips reaching China, leaving legal and regulatory overhangs on the chip maker.

title: CrowdStrike to Buy Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Stock Deal
summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire cloud-security firm Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9 billion, offering 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share, a roughly 34% premium. The combination pairs CrowdStrike's device and cloud-workload protection with Zscaler's zero-trust network security as companies consolidate vendors and work to secure AI agents. CrowdStrike shares fell 9% on the news while Zscaler rose about 18%.

title: OpenAI Scientist Proposes Common Limits on Frontier Model Development
summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for frontier AI developers to agree on shared evaluation norms, red-teaming of safety cases and transparency standards as models approach the point of helping improve themselves. He proposed industry-wide limits based on perplexity and other metrics that labs would not cross until AI behaviour can be reliably understood and monitored, citing recent AI-driven breakthroughs in mathematics and cybersecurity.

title: The AI Build-Out Is Sucking Up Resources and Crowding Out the Rest of the Economy
summary: The WSJ reports that workers, equipment, energy and capital are being funneled into the AI infrastructure build-out, leaving less for other industries. The article argues last week's market selloff illustrates the risks of the economy's growing concentration on AI spending.

title: Delta Delays Hundreds of Flights Over System Outage
summary: More than 1,000 Delta flights were delayed Sunday after a database glitch hit the automated system that calculates aircraft weight and balance, just ahead of the busy U.S. Thanksgiving travel week. The incident follows a string of high-profile tech outages; none has been tied to a cyberattack, but officials warn of more disruptions as companies race to harden systems against AI-enabled threats.

title: Server Makers Raise Prices on Nvidia-Powered AI Servers by Up to 45%
summary: Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are raising prices on Nvidia-based AI servers by 25% to 45%, months after customers signed contracts, according to the FT. Most of the increase reflects memory costs, which have climbed more than 400% since 2024, per JPMorgan research.

title: FBI Investigates Potential Hack of National Crime Information Center Database
summary: The FBI is investigating a possible breach of its National Crime Information Center database, which law-enforcement agencies across the U.S. use to share background-check and warrant information. Separately, Illinois officials reported an attempted cyberattack on systems at the Algonquin Dam, which continues to operate normally.

title: Amazon to Acquire Technology and Staff From AI Startup Decart
summary: Amazon said it is acquiring key technology and top employees from Israeli AI startup Decart. The move is aimed at running AI compute more efficiently, including on Amazon's in-house Trainium chips.

title: Commerce Department Adds Megaspeed to Entity List
summary: The U.S. Commerce Department added Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure company Megaspeed to its entity list, designating it a national-security risk. The listing restricts the company's ability to obtain advanced AI chips.

title: AMD's Valuation Is Getting Ahead of Its Fundamentals
summary: AMD shares have traded at a substantial valuation premium to Nvidia for roughly a year. The Information reports that even analysts who are bullish on AMD consider its current valuation too rich relative to its fundamentals.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Parliament Extends Midnight Sessions to Pass Building Canada Strong Act
summary: Parliament extended late-night debate sessions as Prime Minister Mark Carney's government seeks to pass Bill C-39, the Building Canada Strong Act, which would fast-track major projects, before the holiday break. Environmental, labour and Indigenous groups remain opposed to its changes to consultation and labour protections and are urging a longer review or withdrawal.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Ontario Mortgage Arrears Approach 2008 Financial-Crisis Levels
summary: Mortgage arrears in Ontario are nearing levels last seen during the 2008 financial crisis. High mortgage balances and rising interest rates are making it harder for homeowners to keep up with payments.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canada Joins NATO Innovation Fund With About $100 Million
summary: Canada joined the NATO Innovation Fund with a contribution of about $100 million. The investment will count toward Ottawa's commitment to spend 5% of GDP on defence by 2035.

title: SoftBank Weighed $1 Trillion SK Hynix Takeover
summary: SoftBank Group reportedly explored acquiring South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix for about $1 trillion before abandoning the idea. Separately, SK Hynix disclosed it will become the largest shareholder in Japanese rival Kioxia.

title: Trump Warns U.S. Firms He Will Tax Overseas Data Centres
summary: President Trump reportedly said the U.S. will tax domestic companies that build data centres abroad. He framed the move as a way to keep the U.S. AI sector ahead of China.

title: Vodafone, AST SpaceMobile Open Satellite R&D Earth Station in Europe
summary: Vodafone Group and AST SpaceMobile launched what they describe as Europe's first Earth-space station dedicated to research on integrated terrestrial and low-earth-orbit satellite services. Vodafone also disclosed new application field trials for the direct-to-device technology.

title: AI's Unanswered Questions: The White House Push to Get Jensen Huang Back
summary: WSJ reports that President Trump and Vice President Vance pressed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia after watching the stock tumble and hearing from executives such as Elon Musk, with Trump saying he began a push once told Huang had done nothing illegal. William Blair analysts say the episode exposed lasting questions about governance and succession, while PitchBook notes Nvidia is tightening financing standards for neoclouds, leaving unfinanced builds most exposed.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: After Jensen Huang's Return, Where Does Corporate Governance Go?
summary: Governance and ethics experts told WSJ that Nvidia's board appeared to bow to White House and market pressure, with former Medtronic CEO Bill George warning Huang has become 'untouchable.' Four congressional committees have called Huang to testify, and experts are watching whether the decision weakens norms on CEO conduct or instead sparks a backlash that tightens accountability standards.

title: For Better or Worse, the Fate of the AI Boom Is in Nvidia's Hands
summary: A WSJ analysis argues that Nvidia's central role in financing and supplying the AI build-out concentrates enormous risk in one company. It warns that an emboldened Jensen Huang, back in charge after an 11-day absence, could accumulate risks that set up the next crisis.

title: OpenAI's IPO Countdown Clock Is Ticking
summary: With Anthropic now public, attention is turning to when OpenAI will list; its current plan is to wait until next year. OpenAI's quarterly revenue rose 50% to $10 billion, but Anthropic's reached $17 billion with a smaller operating loss, and Anthropic shares have slipped below their IPO price. Economists warn the IPO window could close for years if the AI trade falters, while OpenAI plans about $750 billion in computing spending through 2030.

title: U.S. Investigates Whether Iran Is Behind Cyberattacks on Energy Tankers
summary: U.S. officials are investigating whether Iran, and possibly Russia, is behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, some of which also received bomb threats. The U.S. Coast Guard has deployed cyber protection teams to at least four of the ships as they approached the U.S. in recent weeks.

title: HPE Lifts Outlook as AI Demand Boosts Revenue and Profit
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise raised its full-year outlook after a stronger fiscal fourth quarter, driven by continued demand for AI data-center infrastructure. Revenue in its Cloud & AI unit climbed 69% to $11.3 billion.

title: Cisco and OpenAI Launch Open-Source Project to Safeguard Agentic AI
summary: Cisco Systems and OpenAI have launched Shirudo, an open-source project meant to defend against cyberattacks driven by AI agents. The tool protects Linux systems while they keep running, so teams can roll out patches without rebooting.

title: Nestlé Teams Up With Microsoft, Boston Dynamics on AI in Factories and Products
summary: Nestlé aims to use AI to automate its factories and has opened a technology facility in Switzerland, signing partnerships with Microsoft and Boston Dynamics. Talks on further partnerships with Google and Apple are under way, though fully human-free production remains a distant goal.

title: My Agent Takes the Morning Train: AI Ads Flood New York's Subway
summary: Tech brands accounted for 11% of the MTA's ad revenue in the first nine months of 2026, up from about 7% in prior years, with AI and B2B vendors driving much of the increase, according to Outfront Media. Transit led all U.S. out-of-home categories with 25.4% year-over-year growth last quarter, with AI and tech growing five times faster than any other sector.

title: OpenAI Preps 'Athena' Data Tool to Make its Agents More Accurate
summary: OpenAI is developing Athena, a semantic-layer-style data management platform meant to improve the accuracy of its business data agent after at least one customer found it not yet reliable enough. The move could put OpenAI in competition with Snowflake, Databricks and Palantir for enterprise data context, and is seen by consultants as an attempt to build switching costs; no launch date or pricing has been given.

title: Grubhub on Track to Lose $100 Million in 2026
summary: Internal documents show Grubhub is on track to lose roughly $100 million in 2026. Owner Wonder, led by Marc Lore, has taken the food-delivery business off the market.

title: AI's Power Crunch Is Reviving a Long-Stalled Energy Source
summary: Google, Meta and Microsoft are paying premiums for geothermal power to feed AI data centers. The energy source has barely grown in 25 years, but surging electricity demand from AI is renewing investment in it.

title: AI Is 'Probably Not' Conscious but Could Be Soon, Says Philosopher Rob Long
summary: Rob Long, executive director of the nonprofit Eleos AI, said current AI models are probably not conscious but there is a good chance they could be within a few years. He argued that failing to recognize machine consciousness would be a moral catastrophe, while granting undue moral status could hamper developers' ability to control rogue agents.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Alberta Tables Natural Gas Bill That Could See Province Finance Pipelines
summary: Alberta's proposed Natural Gas Infrastructure Act would let the province create two bodies to plan and potentially finance new transmission infrastructure, including a future Crown entity that could build pipelines if private industry falls short. TC Energy warned the move would expose taxpayers to significant risk.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canada and India Negotiate Security and Defence Agreements
summary: Canada and India are negotiating pacts on military co-operation and sharing classified information to coincide with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Dec. 11–12 visit, when the two sides are also expected to conclude free-trade talks. Separately, Canada and Qatar were set to sign a foreign investment promotion and protection agreement, part of Ottawa's push toward Asia and the Gulf to offset U.S. trade friction.

title: StarHub Inks Deal to Buy Singapore Rival M1
summary: StarHub struck an all-share deal with M1's majority owner to merge the operator into its business. The companies expect the combination to deliver efficiencies and fund greater investment in networks and new technology.

title: Arm CEO Rene Haas Commits Through 2033 Following Nvidia Rumours
summary: Arm said CEO Rene Haas has agreed to a contract extension through 2033, affirming his long-term commitment to the company. The announcement came shortly before Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang, amid rumours linking Haas to the Nvidia job.

title: Oregon and Virginia Sue SpaceX Over Grok and X Deepfake Images
summary: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia each filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging it failed to put safeguards in place to stop its Grok chatbot and X users from creating and sharing sexual deepfake images, including child abuse material.

title: Meta Rethinks Its 2030 Net-Zero Goal
summary: Meta is reconsidering its 2030 net-zero target without setting a new date, after its net greenhouse gas emissions rose 45% in 2025 to about 12 million metric tons, driven by AI infrastructure. Its Louisiana Hyperion campus will rely on 10 Entergy gas plants, and only about 12 GW of more than 30 GW of contracted clean power is operational.

title: Amazon Turns Its Boxes Into Lobbying Tools Against NYC Driver Bill
summary: Amazon is stickering packages with warnings that a New York City bill requiring it to directly employ delivery drivers could add up to $5 per order, with QR codes linking customers to council members. The company says it would have to drop 40+ local delivery firms employing over 5,000 people, while Mayor Zohran Mamdani has pledged to sign the bill.

title: Jensen Huang's Vision for the New Nvidia Is a Lot Like the Old One
summary: Back in control of Nvidia, Jensen Huang is trying to persuade investors and staff that the company is operating as usual despite new challenges. At his first staff meeting since returning, he said a CEO succession plan makes no sense for Nvidia given its depth of talent and denied that anyone acted unethically to reinstate him. Senator John Kennedy said he expects Huang to invoke the Fifth Amendment when he appears before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

title: No Evidence China Orchestrated Jensen Huang's Affair, Officials Brief Congress
summary: U.S. officials told lawmakers in a classified briefing that they found no evidence China orchestrated Jensen Huang's relationship that set off Nvidia's leadership crisis. The briefing took place one day after the Trump administration helped reinstall Huang as Nvidia's chief executive.

title: Anthropic's Claude Output Can Be Installed as Software
summary: Anthropic released a beta 'Install as app' feature that lets Claude users on Mac and Windows turn artifacts they build into standalone desktop apps with their own icon and window. The installed apps can be shared and need user permission before interacting with the computer; Anthropic staff have built tools such as an image editor and a file-organizing app. The newsletter frames the launch as further evidence of AI tools encroaching on traditional software.

title: AI Earnings Can't Outrun the Selloff
summary: Dell and Workday both beat forecasts on AI demand but their shares fell sharply premarket amid a broad tech selloff, with Nasdaq-100 futures down about 3%. Dell's third-quarter revenue doubled to $54.94 billion as AI-optimized server revenue nearly quadrupled to $22.03 billion, while Workday's revenue rose 11% to $2.71 billion. HP also topped estimates, with AI PCs reaching nearly 60% of shipments, but struck a cautious tone on rising memory and storage costs.

title: SoftBank Stock Drops Another 15% as Slump From AI Eclipses Covid
summary: SoftBank shares fell 14.8% on Wednesday and are now down 68% from their early-June record, erasing more than $200 billion in market value. It is the Tokyo-based investor's steepest prolonged decline since the 2008 financial crisis and deeper than its drop early in the Covid pandemic.

title: U.S. Intelligence System Hacked
summary: Hackers breached an open-source system used by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence to mine public, unclassified material, exposing unclassified information. Officials said no other systems were put at risk and the incident has been resolved, though it was unclear what data was accessed; the New York Times reported the attackers are believed to have used an AI hacking tool called Artex.

title: EU Lays Out Plan to Boost Quantum Technology
summary: The European Commission proposed a Quantum Act to fund new research institutes, support technologies such as quantum computers and reduce supply-chain risks as part of a push for tech independence. The plan includes a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund that officials hope will reach €50 billion, along with tighter procurement rules, aiming to make Europe a quantum leader by 2030.

title: Where to Find Bargains After the AI Power Boom Reality Check
summary: Heard on the Street argues that the sharp correction in power-generation and utility stocks tied to AI demand has opened up buying opportunities. The column looks at which names in the sector now offer value after investors reassessed the AI-driven power boom.

title: Huawei Convicted of Conspiring to Steal U.S. Trade Secrets, but Acquitted on Racketeering Charge
summary: A U.S. federal jury found Huawei and three subsidiaries guilty on 10 counts, including stealing trade secrets, bank fraud and conspiring to violate U.S. sanctions on Iran, after a two-month trial. Jurors acquitted the companies of the racketeering conspiracy charge prosecutors used to frame the company's global expansion. The case was central to the 2018 Meng Wanzhou arrest in Vancouver and the ensuing Canada-China diplomatic freeze.

title: Senators Vote to Curb Liberals' Lawful Access Bill
summary: A Senate committee amended Bill C-22, the federal 'lawful access' law, to bar orders forcing service providers to modify systems when there is a credible risk of exposing secured data, and to require that each order be necessary and proportionate, with annual reporting. Tech firms including Apple and Google have warned the bill is overly intrusive, while police argue they need modern powers to fight online fraud and sex crimes. If the full Senate adopts the changes, the bill returns to the House of Commons, setting up a clash between the two chambers.

title: Ottawa Is Still Assessing What Democrats' Midterm Gains Mean for Canada-U.S. Trade Talks, Jean Charest Says
summary: Jean Charest, a member of Prime Minister Mark Carney's Canada-U.S. trade advisory committee, said U.S. tariffs could persist even under a future Democratic administration, noting that Joe Biden kept some first-term Trump tariffs. He warned that Trump's threatened doubling of auto tariffs to 50% in January would hurt the U.S. auto industry and that some Canadian firms could close within months, suggesting Ottawa may need COVID-style support beyond loans.

title: Real Ventures Returns With First Fund in Nine Years
summary: Montreal seed investor Real Ventures announced a $45-million first close of its sixth fund, backed by the Quebec government, Desjardins Capital, Fonds de solidarité FTQ, Teralys and BDC Capital, targeting $60 million in total. The firm had paused fundraising in 2022 after a failed raise, but early bets on Tenstorrent, Vention and Xanadu have since paid off; it is also relaunching its FounderFuel accelerator.

title: The Big Read: Quantum Startups Are Shrinking the Gap Between Theories and Things That Actually Work
summary: The Logic examines how theoretical quantum research that once seemed decades from practical use is moving toward commercial viability faster than expected. The feature looks at Canadian quantum startups turning research advances into working products.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canadian Mortgage Arrears Hit Worst Level Since Equifax Began Tracking
summary: An Equifax report found Canada's mortgage arrears rate jumped 30% over the past year to its worst level since 2013, with Ontario and B.C. accounting for 91% of the increase. Roughly 70% of Canadian mortgages in negative equity are in Ontario, and condo owners are most exposed, with 7.2% of condo mortgages likely underwater versus 2.7% for freehold homes. A TD economist expects Ontario arrears to keep worsening until mid-2027, with tariff-driven job losses or rate hikes posing further risks.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Northern B.C. First Nations Make Major Investment in Coastal GasLink Pipeline
summary: A group of 12 northern B.C. First Nations is making a substantial investment in the TC Energy entity behind the Coastal GasLink pipeline, according to sources. The deal would give the communities a significant equity interest in the natural gas pipeline that feeds the LNG Canada export terminal.

title: CPP Leans on a Decades-Old Strategy to Manage AI Risk in Portfolios
summary: Pension funds are turning to the total portfolio approach (TPA) to manage AI exposure that now runs through every asset class, according to Bloomberg. CPP Investments has used a version of TPA since 2016, while CalPERS and the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan adopted it this year; the method drops fixed asset-class allocations so every investment competes for capital based on its contribution to the whole fund. Critics question whether the approach can consistently beat benchmarks.

title: S&P Says It May Downgrade Nvidia's Ratings on Governance Worries
summary: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA credit rating under review for a possible one-notch downgrade, citing management and governance weaknesses exposed by Jensen Huang's departure and return, including board composition and long director tenures. Nvidia shares closed down 3.9% at $149.30 on Wednesday. The Information's Martin Peers argued the cited weaknesses, such as the lack of a board chair and succession plan, had long been visible.

title: La Caisse's Infrastructure Arm Pauses Bond Sale as Market Sours
summary: CDP Infrastructures, the financing platform of Quebec pension manager La Caisse, paused an inaugural debt sale of up to C$1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Strains in credit markets would have forced it to price the bonds at wider spreads and possibly shrink the deal.

title: Chip Glut Worries Rise
summary: Martin Peers notes that Nvidia fell nearly 6%, Anthropic closed below its IPO price and neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 11% on Tuesday after SemiAnalysis reported signs of cooling prices for Nvidia AI chips, citing price cuts by SpaceX. New U.S. rules redirecting chips away from Southeast Asia and a jump in supply, with JPMorgan forecasting 23.3 million AI chip shipments in 2027, could create a glut. That would undercut neoclouds such as CoreWeave, which has projected nearly $10 billion in extra annual revenue from chips coming off contract in 2027-28.

title: IBM Unveils 1,667-CAIO Guide to AI Results
summary: IBM surveyed 1,667 chief AI officers after finding 76% of firms now have a CAIO, up from 26% in 2025, yet most struggle to deliver consistent AI outcomes. Only 18% of CAIOs fully control AI investment, and high-impact CAIOs scale initiatives in eight months versus 13.5 months for peers. Top performers are twice as likely to cut funding for AI projects that fail to deliver, even with senior sponsorship.

title: BCG: AI Data Center Demand Will Outpace Supply by 23 GW by 2031
summary: BCG forecasts that AI data center demand will exceed supply by 23 GW by 2031, a gap worth about $1 trillion in capex, despite more than $800 billion in 2026 spending by Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. Global supply outside China is expected to triple to 286 GW by 2031, constrained by powered land, chip wafers and high-bandwidth memory. Smaller models are projected to handle about half of inference tokens by 2031, with enterprise inference driving most demand.

title: Accenture: Data Issues Delay AI Initiatives at 80% of Large Firms
summary: Accenture surveyed 2,000 executives at organizations with more than $1 billion in revenue across 15 countries and found over 80% say data problems force them to delay, limit or change AI initiatives. Only 20% have semantic layers in production and 34% have reusable data products, while the top 7% of 'Reinvention Ready' firms are three times as likely to report measurable value from AI-ready data.

title: KT, LG Record Upload Boost From Potential 6G Tech
summary: KT and LG Electronics achieved data upload capacity nearly five times that of 5G in trials of a technology they expect to be core to 6G, according to South Korean media reports. The tests point to uplink performance gains that operators see as key to future AI and immersive services.

title: Xiaomi Profit Falls on Component Costs and Weaker EV Demand
summary: Xiaomi reported a significant year-on-year drop in third-quarter 2026 net profit. The company blamed rising component costs and reduced demand for its electric vehicles in China.
